order: Phases go from easiest and lowest risk to hardest and riskiest. main stays the stable, playable build while risky work for the next phase happens on a branch.
releaseApproach: main is always the stable, playable build, and game night runs on it.
Each finished phase gets a git tag (v1, v2, ...).
Risky phase work happens on branches and merges into main only when green and playtested.

phases.name: Open the doors
phases.aim: A game that runs, looks decent, and friends can playtest together.

goals.text: Direct peer-to-peer co-op with room codes (1–4 players)
Cozy look, group A: café diorama scene
Cozy look, group B: HUD, night screen, title, menus and lobby
Roadmap drawer on the title screen + suggestion flow
Deployed on GitHub Pages; join with a link and a room code
First game night: 4 friends finish a week (carried over to the next game night)

phases.doneWhen: 4 friends in 4 homes finish a full 7-day week with no crash or desync, and 3+ say it looks like a real game.

phases.name: Busy season
phases.aim: Make the rush fun, chaotic and replayable, in the Overcooked spirit, and let bots fill empty stations. Lowest risk: new content on systems that already work.

goals.text: Day events: rush hour, health inspector, power flicker, influencer visit
40+ cards with combos and synergies (52 cards, 8 sets with pair and full-set bonuses)
Better customers: impatient regulars, big group orders
Difficulty pacing across the week
Sound and juice: dings, steam, coin pops, spill shake
Scripted station bots (no AI model) fill empty stations
Bots feel human: random 0.5–2 s reaction delay, 5–10% mistakes they notice and remake
Bots path around players and stations, and sometimes hesitate or yield when a player is in their way (no new player-to-player collision for humans; revisit after playtests)
Bot personalities (speed, accuracy, focus); more mistakes under rush pressure
One bot-skill difficulty dial, from clumsy to sharp
Telemetry: the host records the run (seed, inputs, snapshots) plus peers' UI events, and downloads one JSON-lines file at run end for the design-analysis agent (no new accounts)
Balance pass
End-of-week awards ceremony, crew stats and lifetime café records
Daily challenges, week difficulty curve and two Easter egg packs

phases.doneWhen: The crew asks to play a second week unprompted, weeks feel different from each other, and 2 players plus 1 bot can finish a week with the bot feeling helpful but not perfect. The first game night's telemetry file has been reviewed by the analysis agent.

phases.name: Real-life growth
phases.aim: A progression that feels like running a real café, with saves that carry over.

goals.text: Barista roles: Chef, Creator, Host, Manager
Per-item pricing with demand that reacts to price
Regulars with favourite drinks
Supplies that spoil (milk, pastries)
Recipe-accuracy stars
Hidden taste map: discover star combos by serving
Signature drink designer
Taste seasons that drift every three days
Rival Starbuck$: scout them; they copy and undercut you
Parody ads tab (Palm Book and friends)
"Pitch an idea" with a scripted keyword judge (no AI)
Checkout path: register → kiosk → Squarely tap terminal
Upgrade path: stand → cart → café
Feedback round 1: readable nights, longer or relaxed nights, bigger order tickets
Feedback round 1: close the day early, sold-out walk-ups, rush hour fix
Station slots: swap stations, extra grinders and espresso machines (replaces the layout editor)
Bots that use the new systems (hurried bots, night tips)
Gear Tree: start with a folding table and $120, buy each machine, learn drinks by making them (v3.0.0)
Bots become hired staff with wages
Saves and unlocks carried between runs

phases.doneWhen: A run feels like "we started tiny and built something", every locked night tab is live, and saves survive a refresh and a new game night with no lost progress.

phases.name: Franchise & rivals
phases.aim: Bigger games across several cafés and game nights. Big new systems, but still predictable code we can test.

goals.text: Rival escalation: Starbuck$ grows with you from week 2
Campus franchise of several cafés
Manager mode: assign crews, read reports
Phone calls and travel between sites
2v2 rival chains on a shared street, competing for the same customers
Seasons that carry across game nights

phases.doneWhen: 4 players finish a 2v2 match with a results screen, and the crew plays one season across 2+ game nights without a save problem.

phases.name: Smart café
phases.aim: AI makes the café feel alive, as an option and never required. Hardest phase: outside services, real costs, unpredictable answers.

goals.text: AI modes: Off / Lite / Full
LLM dialogue: customers, staff and bot personalities that talk
AI pitch judge, with the scripted judge as fallback
Creative out-of-scope player actions, bounded by the rules
Server-side backend that keeps API keys safe, capped per room per day
Scripted bots still make the drinks; the LLM never does split-second station work
AI never blocks play: scripted fallbacks everywhere

phases.doneWhen: 1 human plus 3 AI teammates finish a week under budget (< $20/month total), and switching AI off changes nothing else.

phases.name: Polish
phases.aim: Make everything we built solid and smooth.

goals.text: Bug-fix pass from the playtest backlog
Visual passes
Performance on older laptops
Save cleanup and migration

phases.doneWhen: A full game night runs on the stable build with zero known crash bugs, steady frame rate on every friend's machine, and old saves still load.

changelog.text: UI overhaul round 1: cozy diorama café scene
Roadmap reordered into 6 phases by difficulty; scripted station bots moved to Phase 2
Telemetry restored to Phase 2: host-recorded run log and peer UI events, downloaded as a file; no new accounts
Phase 2 sim side: pass, menu switch, day events, customer kinds, scripted bots, telemetry, balance tester
Chaos pack sim side: drop key, floor messes, mop and cleanliness, rogue customer
Awards ceremony, crew stats and café records
Balance pass: cheaper upgrades, full card sets, fittings count in your score
Version 2.1.0: Phase 3 preview is live (roles, pricing, taste map, signature, rival, ads, pitch, checkout, growth)
Feedback round 1 planned from Kennedy's first Phase 3 playtest
Version 2.2.0: Feedback round 1 (readable nights, close early, sold-out walk-ups, station slots, bot tips)
Version 3.0.0: the Gear Tree. Every run starts tiny and buys its bar one machine at a time
Version 3.1.0: Phase 3 is done. Hired staff with wages, and head starts carried between runs
